text: Compose with the selected communicative playbook; keep that family in playbook. Use direction-contract.md without new account fields or opaque IDs. Read account-identity-composition for asset selection and identity treatment. This skill owns the account argument.

Separate the context before writing: Advertiser (who speaks, kit, evidence, voice); Target identity (exact name/domain and the source that identifies it — an ambiguous name needs an identity gap); Account facts (only supplied or retrieved evidence); Persona/use-case hypothesis (an assumption); Campaign intent; Relationship evidence (co-placement establishes no relationship).
Put actual source descriptions/excerpts in evidence and bind factual copy through evidence_refs. Bare claim IDs without accessible values/evidence cannot support copy.

Scope personalization to the request: for an explicitly logo-only or exact-copy adaptation, preserve the approved message and record identity-only scope; for requested audience/use-case relevance, join a supported advertiser capability to that audience … Without account research, phrase this as an invitation or proposed use.

Reading the account: read_project_accounts(query=…) and page with offset; never guess a domain or a logo for an account you did not find. read_account_research(…, section="overview"), then section="claims" (pages via next_offset); account_not_researched → say so in review_needs. read_claims for a specific question.
note: Second home of the account-reads procedure (A1 step 2 names it, D6 describes the tools).

text: Put what you read into evidence and bind copy through evidence_refs with the claim id … A fact you did not read is not a fact. An empty field is an honest answer; narrow the message rather than fill the gap. A read costs nothing and starts no research.

Carry the argument in artwork, requested companion copy, or both … Remove the company name and logo mentally: identify what audience/task makes the message relevant. If only the name changed, repair the argument or record the unmet request in review_needs.
An invitation is a scope of intent, not mandatory wording. Write natural useful copy; keep internal phrases such as "an invitation for [company] marketers" in assumptions.
Audit advertiser promises separately from target facts: imperatives still imply capabilities. Coverage, after-hours availability, compatibility and results need their own evidence.
note: Same rule as D1 L37 (positioning / imperative grammar).

text: For a new account message, construct the argument before choosing a headline: 1 reader and task (keep the target team distinct from its customers) … 2 one evidenced advertiser mechanism … 3 a concrete proposition … 4 choose what the reader should see (authentic product, native diagram, artwork, type-led emphasis).
A logo and decorative connector alone explain no product mechanism … imagery remains optional unless requested. Judge whether the visible relationship makes this argument clearer.

Name-removal test … Different accounts may share a useful task; do not invent distinctions or force new wording merely to make variants look researched. Explicit exact-copy and identity-only requests retain their original message.

When adapting approved creative, inspect its current scene and view its render. For variants, put the advertiser kit, effective type, palette and successful message/artwork groups in preserve, with intended changes in vary … Recompose and remeasure for longer target names or different images … Vary messaging only when evidence changes the argument.
Preserve the advertiser's voice, palette and visual system unless a deliberate departure is requested.
note: The strongest brand-fidelity rule in the harness, but it lives only in the account skill. The revamp read this skill and still swapped the pastel look; "unless a deliberate departure is requested" let "make it more premium" count as a departure.

text: Choose the identity treatment through the supporting skill rather than treating a logo row as the creative concept.
CTA presence follows the actual next step; an awareness ad need not have one.

The direction's copy contains only native artwork text … Keep requested companion channel copy out of the image; label it separately in the finalize_run summary … Never report it published or claim delivery through an unreviewed or failed handoff.
Review the complete argument under review.md: exact identity, relationship implications, evidence-scoped copy, placement-size reading order, logo pixels, editable layers and preserved properties.
Engine audience/slot operations are primitives; this skill provides neither a connected account picker nor all-account content scaling. Report only the variants actually made and reviewed.
